dedupe_keys.name: effect of strain history on cone penetration resistance and cyclic strength of saturated sand

description: Effect of strain history on cone penetration resistance and cyclic strength of saturated sand is a dataset listed in DesignSafe Data Depot (published projects), a research data repository for natural hazards engineering under the section "experimental", published or maintained by Ross Boulanger, University of California Davis (ucdavis.edu). This series of tests demonstrate the use of dynamic centrifuge model testing to develop CPT based correlations for the cyclic strength of soil. Level profiles of saturated Ottawa sand were subjected to multiple shaking events until the models were no longer liquefiable. Coverage: as described in the project (site or event named in the description). DesignSafe files it as a "experimental" project. Its DOI is 10.17603/DS24T25. Keywords: centrifuge, liquefaction, repeated shaking, cone penetration resistances, sand. Published 2018-04-26. It is reached through the links recorded on this page, with the catalogue entry as the discovery route. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is not stated in the DesignSafe listing (publication licences offered are CC BY 4.0, ODC-By, CC0 and GPL; project page not read). Caveats: this record was written from the catalogue listing only, so the linked page was not opened, its contents and current availability were not checked, and the description may lag the source. It can support structural performance, hazard exposure and resilience studies. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-designsafe-data-depot-repository.
